memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: and he said to Moses, "Please, my lord, I ask you not to hold against us the sin we have so foolishly committed. Do not let her be like a stillborn infant coming from its mother's womb with its flesh half eaten away." So Moses cried out to the Lord, "Please, God, heal her!" — Num 12:11-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron's proud complaint collapses into a desperate plea. Just moments ago he was questioning Moses' authority; now he begs the very brother he wronged for help. "Please, my lord," he says, calling Moses by the title he had resented. Sin has a way of humbling us in the end.

Notice Aaron's honesty. He does not make excuses or shift the blame. He calls it what it is: "the sin we have so foolishly committed." True repentance names the wrong plainly rather than softening it. Aaron owns it fully, and that honesty is the beginning of restoration.

But the most beautiful thing here is Moses' response. The man who was slandered, criticised, and undermined does not gloat or demand an apology. He immediately cries out, "Please, God, heal her!" Seven simple words, full of grace. Moses returns love for injury and mercy for malice.

This is the very heart of the gospel lived out. Moses interceding for the sister who wronged him is a small picture of Christ, who prayed "Father, forgive them" for those who crucified Him. Jesus does not wait for us to grovel adequately before He intercedes; He pleads for us even in our foolishness. And He calls us to the same grace — to pray for those who hurt us, to forgive quickly, to seek the good of those who wrong us. That is what it means to belong to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When someone wrongs you, do you demand apology or offer grace?
2. Does your repentance name sin honestly, as Aaron finally did?
3. Who has hurt you that you could pray for, as Moses prayed for Miriam?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for Christ who intercedes for me even in my foolishness. Give me a heart like Moses that returns grace for injury, and help me to forgive and pray for those who wrong me. Amen.
